The **Yamaha MODX** is a synthesizer keyboard. It has pianos, organs, strings, synths and drum kits built in.
It can also be a **sound card for the computer**. Plug in one USB cable, and the computer can record the
MODX and play sound back through it. You don't need a separate audio interface.

## The parts you'll use

| Part | What it's for |
|---|---|
| **Touch screen** | Choose sounds (a sound is called a *Performance*), change settings |
| **Super Knob** (the big knob) | Changes several settings at once. Turn it while you play to change the sound |
| **Scene buttons** | Up to 8 saved versions of the current sound. Press one to switch |
| **CATEGORY SEARCH** | Find a sound by type: Piano, Keyboard, Organ, Strings, Synth Lead, Drum… |
| **[EXIT]** | Goes back one screen. Press it again and again to get home |
| **Back panel: OUTPUT L/MONO, R** | Two 1/4" jacks to the mixer or speakers. Use only L for mono |
| **Back panel: A/D INPUT** | Plug in a mic or guitar here to send it through the MODX |
| **Back panel: USB TO HOST** | USB cable to the computer, for MIDI and audio |
| **PHONES** | Headphones. Turn the master volume down before you put them on |

## Find a sound

1. Press **[CATEGORY SEARCH]**.
2. Touch a category (for example *Piano*), then touch a sound in the list.
3. Play. Turn the Super Knob to hear how the sound changes.
4. Press **[EXIT]** when you're done.

You don't need to save to play a sound. Save only if you change one and want to keep it.

## Using the MODX as an audio interface

This is the easiest way to record a keyboard part. **One USB cable carries everything:** the notes you play
(MIDI), the sound of the MODX (audio into the computer), and the computer's sound (audio back out of the
MODX's outputs and headphones).

### Setup

1. Connect **USB TO HOST** on the MODX to the computer with a USB cable (USB-A to USB-B).
2. Turn the MODX on.
3. On the computer, open your DAW's audio settings:
   - **Input device:** Yamaha MODX
   - **Output device:** Yamaha MODX
   - **Sample rate:** 44.1 kHz
4. Make an audio track. Set its input to the first stereo pair (1–2). Arm it and press record.
5. Plug headphones into the MODX, or run its outputs to the mixer. You hear the computer and the
   keyboard together, from one place.

That's all. No extra boxes, no extra cables, no mic stand.

### Why it's easy

- **One cable.** A normal setup needs a keyboard, an audio interface, two audio cables and a USB cable. The
  MODX does all of it.
- **Clean sound.** The audio stays digital from the MODX into the computer. Nothing to hum, no gain knob to
  set too high or too low.
- **One place to listen.** The computer's playback comes out of the MODX's headphone jack, so you hear the
  backing track and your playing together, with no lag.
- **Mic or guitar too.** Plug a mic or guitar into **A/D INPUT** and it goes to the computer over the same
  USB cable.

### Things to check if it doesn't work

| Problem | Try |
|---|---|
| The computer doesn't list "Yamaha MODX" | Use a different USB cable (some only charge). Plug straight into the computer, not a hub |
| Windows: no MODX audio device | Install the **Yamaha Steinberg USB Driver** from Yamaha's website |
| You hear yourself twice, a little late | Turn off *input monitoring* on the DAW track. You already hear the MODX directly |
| No sound from the computer | Check the DAW's output device is the MODX, and the MODX master volume is up |
| Recording is silent | Check the track's input is 1–2 and the track is armed |

::: {.callout-note}
**Unverified:** Yamaha community forums disagree on whether a Mac needs the Yamaha driver or works without
one, and on the exact number of USB audio channels (often quoted as 10 out to the computer and 4 back, at
44.1 kHz). Check the MODX Owner's Manual before relying on these.
:::

## Play the site's band on it

The [band section below](#play-the-band-on-the-modx) sends the Backing Track band's notes to the MODX, so its bass, keys, guitar or
drums play on the board instead of in the browser. It compares each sound side by side so you can pick which
instruments to send. If the computer's sound also comes out of the MODX (set the computer's output to the MODX), both
come out of the same speakers, and the timing is easier to line up.

Send the band's notes to a Yamaha MODX over USB instead of playing the site's own samples, one instrument at a time. Works in
Chrome or Edge (Web MIDI). Nothing changes for anyone without a MODX: until you switch it on here, every page sounds as before.
To audition the board's congas, timbales and brushes, see [the percussion auditions below](#percussion-auditions).

```{=html}

  <tr><td>11</td><td>11</td><td>Steel-string acoustic guitar</td><td>acoustic guitar (steel)</td></tr>
  <tr><td>12</td><td>12</td><td>Brush Kit</td><td>drums: brush grooves, and every brush stroke</td></tr>
  <tr><td>13</td><td>13</td><td>BeechwoodSnare Kit</td><td>drums: jazz time, Latin, blues shuffles</td></tr>
  <tr><td>14</td><td>14</td><td>Rock Stereo Kit 1</td><td>drums: rock, half-time, train beat</td></tr>
  <tr><td>15</td><td>15</td><td>Dry Standard Kit</td><td>drums: pop, ballads, dance, Motown, folk</td></tr>
  <tr><td>16</td><td>16</td><td>R&amp;B Kit 1</td><td>drums: funk, reggaeton</td></tr>
</table>
<p class="mx-note">Five drum kits, because one kit made some styles sound wrong. Which groove goes to which kit is set under
<a href="#drum-maps">Drum maps</a>. On R&amp;B Kit 1 the tom keys play 808-style kicks (Data List), so tom fills in funk sound odd.</p>
<p class="mx-note">Then, in Utility → Settings → MIDI, check that the MODX receives Bank Select and Program Change, so the button below
can call the Performance up. Bank and number: in the Performance list, the User bank is shown with the number of each slot.
The defaults below (MSB 63, LSB 32, program 0 = User 1, first slot) are from memory of Yamaha's MIDI tables and not yet checked on the board.</p>
<div class="mx-row">
  <label>Channel <input type="number" id="mx-pch" min="1" max="16"></label>
  <label>Bank MSB <input type="number" id="mx-msb" min="0" max="127"></label>
  <label>LSB <input type="number" id="mx-lsb" min="0" max="127"></label>
  <label>Program <input type="number" id="mx-pc" min="0" max="127"></label>
  <button type="button" id="mx-perf">Call it up</button>
  <label><input type="checkbox" id="mx-perf-auto"> on connect</label>
</div>
```

### Timing

```{=html}
<p>The computer's speakers and the MODX's are late by different amounts. Press Start: the site plays a stick click and the MODX
a rim click at the same time. Move the slider until you hear one click instead of two. Use the speakers or headphones you'll play with.</p>
<div class="mx-row">
  <button type="button" id="mx-sync">Start</button>
  <label>MODX offset <input type="range" id="mx-off" min="-150" max="250" step="1"> <span id="mx-off-n"></span> ms</label>
</div>
<p class="mx-note">More than zero holds the MODX back; less than zero sends it earlier (only as far as the site's own delay allows).</p>
```

### Compare

```{=html}
<p>Each row plays the same phrase twice, the site and then the MODX (with the Site Band Performance loaded), so you can pick
the better one. Your choices are kept. <b>Route the winners</b> sends every instrument where the MODX won to the board.</p>
<div class="mx-row"><button type="button" id="mx-stop">Stop</button> <button type="button" id="mx-win">Route the winners</button> <span id="mx-win-msg" class="mx-note"></span></div>
<table class="mx-table" id="mx-compare"></table>
```

### Routing

```{=html}
<p>Which instruments go to the MODX, and on which channel. Instruments sharing a channel share a Part.</p>
<p class="mx-note"><b>Shift</b> moves an instrument's notes on the way to the MODX: 12 = an octave up, −12 = an octave down. Use it
when a MODX voice sounds an octave off from the site (▶ both plays the site's phrase and then the MODX's). <b>Velocity</b> spreads
the band's soft-to-loud over that range of MIDI velocities: 1–127 sends what the band plays; raising the low number (say 40–120)
keeps a piano or Rhodes out of its dullest, softest layers. Before blaming a voice, check on the board: Utility → Settings → MIDI,
<i>MIDI I/O Mode</i> = Multi (else one channel plays every keyboard Part); Arp Master and each Part's arpeggio and motion sequencer
off; no Note Shift or Note Limit left on a Part; and no Mega Voices — the Reference Manual says they "have a very complex structure
with many different layers that are not suitable for playing manually" and should be played only by their own arpeggios.</p>
<table class="mx-table" id="mx-routes"></table>
<div class="mx-row">
  <label>Pitch-bend range <input type="number" id="mx-pb" min="1" max="24"> semitones</label>
  <label>Rotary speed CC <input type="number" id="mx-les" min="0" max="127"></label>
  <button type="button" id="mx-reset">Reset everything here</button>
</div>
<p class="mx-note">The pitch-bend range must match the Part's (2 is the usual default) or slides land on the wrong note.
The rotary speed CC is what the organ's slow/fast switch sends: 1 (the mod wheel) is a guess, so check which control your organ
Performance uses for it.</p>
```

Loops written for four MODX+ drum kits, sent straight to the board over USB. Use them to hear the congas, bongos, timbales,
bells and brushes, and mark the ones you'd use with ☆. Works in Chrome or Edge (Web MIDI). The key maps come from Yamaha's
MODX6+/7+/8+ Data List (Drum Kit Assign List); each loop says what was checked against a source (listed under Works Cited) and what is still the site's own guess.

Each example below is the Backing Track band in one style. Press ▶ Play, then flip **Site** and **MODX** while it plays
(or press **m**), or tick **Switch every … bars** to hear them take turns. Mark which sounds better under each one; the
tally is at the top. The MODX plays each instrument on its Part of the Site Band Performance and the drums on the kit for
that style (set on [the band section above](#play-the-band-on-the-modx)); an instrument with no Part stays on the site.

Absil, Frans. "Band Latin." [www.fransabsil.nl/archpdf/bandlatn.pdf](https://www.fransabsil.nl/archpdf/bandlatn.pdf). Forward and reversed (2-3) cáscara side by side.

"Beating the Bongos." *Dummies*, Wiley. [www.dummies.com/article/academics-the-arts/music/instruments/drums/beating-the-bongos-199618/](https://www.dummies.com/article/academics-the-arts/music/instruments/drums/beating-the-bongos-199618/). Martillo: slaps on the small drum, the open tone on the large drum, soft left-hand tones.

"Bell pattern." *Wikipedia*, Wikimedia Foundation, [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bell_pattern](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bell_pattern). The 12/8 standard pattern: 1, 1a, 2&, 2a, 3&, 4, 4a.

"Benny Benjamin." *Rock & Roll Hall of Fame*, 2003. [rockhall.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/Benny_Benjamin_2003.pdf](https://rockhall.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/Benny_Benjamin_2003.pdf). His constant quarter-note snare (seen in search excerpt).

"Bernard Purdie." *Wikipedia*, Wikimedia Foundation, [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernard_Purdie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernard_Purdie). The Purdie shuffle: triplets against a half-time backbeat, ghost notes on the snare.

"Bongo Patterns." [www.lx.iriss.org.uk/read/bongo-patterns.html](https://www.lx.iriss.org.uk/read/bongo-patterns.html). Martillo: eight strokes, accents on 1, 3 and 4, beat 4 on the hembra (seen in search excerpt only; page refused direct reading).

"Boom bap." *Wikipedia*, Wikimedia Foundation, [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boom_bap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boom_bap). Kick on 1 and 3, snare on 2 and 4, highly swung programming on the MPC and SP-1200.

"Brushes." *BYU Percussion*, Brigham Young University. [percussion.byu.edu/brushes](https://percussion.byu.edu/brushes). Swing: right hand swings, left stirs, the hands trade places on 2 and 4; ballads: both hands stir in opposite directions.

"Cascara Rhythms." *Salsa Forums*. [www.salsaforums.com/threads/cascara-rhythms.26232/](https://www.salsaforums.com/threads/cascara-rhythms.26232/). The 3-2 and 2-3 cáscara counts used here (a member's transcription).

"Cascara." *Soundbrenner*. [www.soundbrenner.com/blogs/articles/cascara](https://www.soundbrenner.com/blogs/articles/cascara). Cáscara follows the clave's direction; its printed grid differs from the one used here.

"Disco." *Wikipedia*, Wikimedia Foundation, [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disco). Four-on-the-floor bass drum, 'an open hissing hi-hat on the off-beat'.

"Drum beat." *Wikipedia*, Wikimedia Foundation, [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drum_beat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drum_beat). Straight rock groove (kick and snare on the beats, hats on the eighths); half-time (snare on 3, hats in quarters); the delayed backbeat of funk.

"Four on the floor (music)." *Wikipedia*, Wikimedia Foundation, [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Four_on_the_floor_(music)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Four_on_the_floor_(music)). The bass drum on every beat; disco and dance music.

"Groove: How J Dilla Changed Rhythm." *The Pudding*, June 2023. [pudding.cool/2023/06/groove/](https://pudding.cool/2023/06/groove/). Straight, swung and shifted parts at once; swung (quintuplet) hi-hat, slightly early snare.

"How to Play the Pandeiro for Capoeira." *Dende Arts*. [dendearts.com/blog/how-to-play-the-pandeiro-for-capoeira/](https://dendearts.com/blog/how-to-play-the-pandeiro-for-capoeira/). Thumb, fingertips, heel, fingertips.

"Latin Percussion Applications in the Jazz Band." *Jazz Education Network*. [jazzednet.org/resources/latin-percussion-applications-in-the-jazz-band/](https://jazzednet.org/resources/latin-percussion-applications-in-the-jazz-band/). Cha-cha-chá: bell in quarters, güiro long quarter + two eighths.

"Motown Groove." *Soundbrenner*. [www.soundbrenner.com/blogs/articles/motown-groove](https://www.soundbrenner.com/blogs/articles/motown-groove). Snare on 2 and 4 or on all four beats; tambourine in eighths; kick on 1 and 3.

"New jack swing." *Wikipedia*, Wikimedia Foundation, [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_jack_swing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_jack_swing). Offbeat-accented sixteenth-note triplets; the TR-808 snare; TR-808, LinnDrum, SP-1200.

"The Pandeiro." *Acoustics Today*, July 2007, p. 41. [acousticstoday.org/issues/2007AT/Jul2007/files/basic-html/page41.html](https://acousticstoday.org/issues/2007AT/Jul2007/files/basic-html/page41.html). Pandeiro batida: thumb, fingertips, heel, fingertips.

"Salsa (musical structure)." *Wikipedia*, Wikimedia Foundation, [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salsa_(musical_structure)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salsa_(musical_structure)). Conga marcha (tumbao) and its alignment with clave; the timbale bell from the cáscara.

"Salsa Rhythm: How to Play Tumbao." *Salsa Vida*. [www.salsavida.com/?p=509](https://www.salsavida.com/?p=509). Open tones on 4 and 4&, the slap on 2.

"Timbale: Playing the Son." *Artdrum*. [www.artdrum.com/TIMBALE_PLAYING_THE_SON.HTM](https://www.artdrum.com/TIMBALE_PLAYING_THE_SON.HTM). Paila: left hand muffled on 2, open on 4; the tumbao is the cha-cha-chá conga part, faster.

"Trap music." *Wikipedia*, Wikimedia Foundation, [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trap_music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trap_music). About 140 bpm in half-time, deep 808 kicks with long decay, double- and triple-time hi-hats.

"Tumbao." *Soundbrenner*. [www.soundbrenner.com/blogs/articles/tumbao](https://www.soundbrenner.com/blogs/articles/tumbao). Heel-toe, slap and open tones of the tumbao.

"Tumbao." *Wikipedia*, Wikimedia Foundation, [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tumbao](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tumbao). Cites Rebeca Mauleón, *Salsa Guidebook*.

Yamaha Corporation. *MODX6+ / MODX7+ / MODX8+ Data List*. Yamaha. [usa.yamaha.com/files/download/other_assets/5/1583935/modx_plus_en_dl_a0.pdf](https://usa.yamaha.com/files/download/other_assets/5/1583935/modx_plus_en_dl_a0.pdf). Drum Kit Assign List: the key of every sound in Pop Latin Kit, Real Brushes Kit, Jazz Brushes Kit and Brush Kit (kit-to-table match read from the page layout).

**For students**

"Backbeat." *Wikipedia*, Wikimedia Foundation, [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Backbeat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Backbeat). The backbeat on 2 and 4; the delayed or late backbeat.
